scene: On the pirate sloop's deck at sunset, the Cook (round, red-faced man of about fifty-five, bushy white mustache, thick white eyebrows, no beard, faded red knitted cap, blue-and-white checked shirt, stained cream canvas apron with a wooden ladle tucked in its string, leaning on a walking stick) stands beside a small iron kettle on a box of bricks, holding out one single ladle of water with a fierce, protective face. In front of him a queue of thirsty crewmen holds out tin cups: Tom (navy waistcoat, no hat) at the front with a pleading look, the Captain (black tricorn, full brown beard, burgundy long coat) behind him also waiting his turn. The Quartermaster (dark-brown wavy hair, light stubble, white shirt, dark-brown waistcoat) stands at the cook's side ticking his ledger. Tension: one ladle each, even for the captain.

On a moonlit sandy beach, Tom (navy waistcoat, no hat) sprints after a large sea turtle heading calmly toward the surf, arms out, face desperate, while the Cook (round, red-faced, bushy white mustache, faded red knitted cap, blue-and-white checked shirt, cream canvas apron, walking stick) sits on an upturned bucket beside a small campfire with a cooking pot, watching with a deeply unimpressed face and a wooden ladle in his hand. The pirate sloop is anchored in the bay behind them. Tension: dinner is getting away.
